brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.evidence: Exactly one base stands on the build: piece:0,0,0;half-n (a single half-n hex base, one cell, level 0). It is a half rather than the full hex originally standing, because the configurator offers no drawer socket on a full base at all.

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: No neighbouring, stacked or on-top parts: get_build lists only the one base plus the drawer counted in its parts budget. No props, covers, bins, bolts or extra layers were added; capOpenFaces/lockJoints were deliberately left out as they would add parts.

Only one drawer fits this single base: drawer:0#0,0#cut, the one socket (key 's', the cut face of the half base) that find_sockets offered. A single hex face takes a single drawer; no further drawer socket exists on one base, so four of the five requested drawers cannot be placed. The one drawer placed is a multi-part drawer assembly (5 parts in the print budget: frame, runners and drawer boxes), which is the closest the configurator allows to 'drawers in a single hex base'.

finish.summary: Built the closest layout the configurator accepts: one single hex base (half-n, after swapping the standing full base, which offers no drawer socket at all) with the one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut, a 5-part drawer assembly) fitted to its cut face. Nothing was added beside or on top of the base, and no caps, bolts or props were staged. Five separate drawers cannot fit in a single hex base — the configurator offers exactly one drawer socket per base — so that requirement is unmet and the outcome is a compromise. check_build is clean (meshClash clear; only open-cap-face info, left uncapped to honour 'nothing else added').

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Single hex, five drawers, nothing else — I'll check the current build and what drawer fittings it offers.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
